description: Source-checked public opportunity statements; NOT proof of approval, individual eligibility, settled revenue, or current service availability.

opportunities.anti_leverage: Do not extrapolate these rates to all contractors or convert them into guaranteed revenue. Do not justify AEO spend from low-volume ChatGPT calls; paid search converts better in this report. Track each pilot customer's own qualified inquiries and booked jobs.
opportunities.claim: Invoca's July 2026 home-services report says 38% of calls answered by a person are leads, 45% of those leads convert on the call, and 55% of home-services businesses do not ask leads to buy or book. ChatGPT-referred calls show a 45% lead rate versus 40% for paid search, but a 41% conversion rate versus 48% for paid search; total LLM-attributed call volume is very low and no measurable volume from LLMs other than ChatGPT is reported. The data are averages across Invoca's customer base and nine home-services subindustries within a broader dataset of more than 70 million calls and 600 million minutes.
opportunities.eligibility: Not a grant or product offer; use only as a directional benchmark for home-services call handling and lead conversion.
opportunities.friction: Vendor-owned customer-base averages, not a national probability sample; nine subindustries and varied company sizes; no causal proof that missed-call automation recovers jobs; ChatGPT-attributed call volume remains very low.
opportunities.observed_delta: First journal capture of the report's answered-call lead rate, on-call conversion, ask-to-book gap and ChatGPT referral volume/conversion split; the earlier Invoca record covers answer rates only.
opportunities.title: Invoca 2026 home-services benchmark adds lead and booking outcomes beyond answer rates
opportunities.value: No cash, credits or recovered revenue. Industry benchmark/problem evidence only.
opportunities.why_now: This extends the existing Invoca answer-rate record with lead, on-call conversion and ask-to-book measures. It strengthens the SECONDS MATTER pilot scorecard while correcting a possible AI-search hype signal: a higher lead rate does not imply higher booked-job conversion or meaningful call volume.

opportunities.anti_leverage: Do not pursue the $350,000 headline as if it were a free solo-founder grant. Do not apply until the actual venture intent, working MVP, public website, domain-matched email and billing account requirements are met; no eligibility or approval is assumed.
opportunities.claim: Google's current program FAQ says its Start tier offers $2,000 in Cloud credits for startups founded within the past two years that have a working MVP, a clear business model and plans to seek venture funding soon. The larger Scale and Scale AI tiers advertise $200,000-$350,000 in credits but require verifiable Pre-Seed to Series A funding. Google also requires an active reachable business website describing the company, founder/team and products, a business email matching the website domain, and the correct Google Cloud billing account. The program excludes consultancies, agencies, dev shops and personal blogs, and acceptance is discretionary.
opportunities.eligibility: Start tier: startup founded within two years, working MVP, clear business model, plans to seek venture funding soon, active public business website, matching business email/domain and a Google Cloud billing account. Funded tiers require verifiable Pre-Seed to Series A funding. Agencies, consultancies, dev shops and personal blogs are excluded.
opportunities.friction: Application and credit award are discretionary. Website must be active and describe the business, founder/team and product; placeholder sites are not accepted and Google says high volumes of AI-generated content may be rejected. Third-party models and subscription-billed services are excluded from credits. Domain and billing-account ownership must align.
opportunities.observed_delta: First source-checked entry for the Google for Startups Cloud Program. Captures the current $2,000 Start tier and its venture-intent, MVP, domain-email, website, funding and service exclusions.
opportunities.title: Google for Startups Start tier offers $2,000 credits with venture-intent and public-website gates
opportunities.value: $2,000 in Google Cloud credits for the Start tier, not cash. The $200,000-$350,000 tiers are for funded startups and are not an accessible pre-funded benefit. Credits apply to eligible first-party Google Cloud consumption services, not subscription-billed products or third-party Model Garden/Marketplace services.
opportunities.why_now: This is a newly captured eligibility baseline. The headline maximum can mislead bootstrapped founders: the pre-funded Start tier is $2,000 and still has venture-intent, working-MVP, website and domain-email gates.

opportunities.anti_leverage: Do not retract the earlier GA plan list or assert Free/Team support for this repository without a direct plan-level test or official clarification. Preserve both source URLs and the unresolved discrepancy.
opportunities.claim: The current GitHub Docs how-to page's 'Who can use this feature?' section lists people with write access and GitHub Enterprise Cloud. GitHub's October 28, 2026 GA announcement explicitly lists GitHub Enterprise Cloud, Enterprise Cloud with data residency, Team and Free plans. Both first-party pages are currently accessible and conflict; no evidence of a plan-access change has been established.
opportunities.eligibility: Conflicting first-party documentation: the October 28 GA release note lists Free, Team, Enterprise Cloud and Enterprise Cloud with data residency; the current how-to eligibility panel lists Enterprise Cloud only. Availability on this specific repository's plan has not been tested.
opportunities.friction: No .github/workflows/actions.lock file was found on the research branch and no plan-level feature test was run. The how-to page's eligibility panel may be stale or incomplete; it does not by itself establish a restriction.
opportunities.observed_delta: Due recheck found a current first-party docs conflict: the GA announcement includes Free and Team, while the how-to page's eligibility panel only names Enterprise Cloud. No product availability change is confirmed.
opportunities.title: GitHub workflow lockfile plan-eligibility documentation conflicts with the GA release note
opportunities.value: No cash or credits. This is a GitHub Actions supply-chain security feature that pins action dependencies to reviewed commits.
opportunities.why_now: The scheduled recheck was due November 12. The current how-to page conflicts with the prior source-checked GA announcement and the existing ledger eligibility claim, so the discrepancy is recorded rather than silently changing the historical record.

opportunities.anti_leverage: Do not add a paid Workers plan or deploy this for a speculative experiment. Do not expose it without Access. Treat it as a watchlist component until compatibility, cost and source-verification reliability are tested.
opportunities.claim: Cloudflare's Kitesurf repository is public under Apache 2.0 and describes an experimental browser engine for AI agents that parses HTML, applies CSS, runs page JavaScript, renders screenshots without Chrome, and supports CDP clients such as Puppeteer. The README says self-hosted Cloudflare deployment requires Workers Paid because Kitesurf uses Dynamic Workers; local development uses wrangler dev. The engine has no built-in authentication and a deployed workers.dev URL is public by default unless protected with Cloudflare Access or another authentication layer.
opportunities.eligibility: Public repository can be inspected and locally developed. The README lists Node.js 22+, pnpm 9.15.4, Bazelisk/Bazel and a Rust/WebAssembly build. Running a self-hosted instance on Cloudflare requires Workers Paid.
opportunities.friction: Experimental compatibility and reliability; first local build compiles Rust/WebAssembly with Bazel; Workers Paid required for cloud deployment; no built-in authentication; exposed deployment can allow arbitrary browser/CDP use and outbound requests billed to the owner's Cloudflare account. Release note: https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-11-12-kitesurf-open-source/.
opportunities.observed_delta: Newly open-sourced agent browser engine; the material access constraints are Workers Paid for self-hosting, experimental status, a substantial local build toolchain, and no built-in authentication.
opportunities.title: Cloudflare opens Kitesurf agent browser under Apache 2.0, but self-hosting requires Workers Paid
opportunities.value: No cash or credits. Source code is available under Apache 2.0; no measured cost saving is established, and self-hosted Cloudflare deployment requires a Workers Paid plan.
opportunities.why_now: Cloudflare announced the open-source release on November 12-13, 2026. This is a potentially reusable browser-verification component for agent workflows, but its actual deployment and security costs are material for a near-zero-budget, cloud-first founder.

opportunities.anti_leverage: Do not create or fund a founder-owned multi-customer telecom account as a shortcut. Have each customer own its business messaging registration and number where feasible, or explicitly pass through costs after consent. Do not promise production SMS until the required brand and campaign are approved. Do not use the stale $4/$44 comparison figures.
opportunities.claim: Twilio's current U.S. A2P 10DLC fee article lists Sole Proprietor Brand registration at $4.50 one-time for individuals and small businesses without an EIN; Low Volume Standard Brand registration at $4.50 for EIN businesses with low traffic; and Standard Brand registration at $46 one-time, including $41.50 secondary vetting, for higher-volume EIN businesses. Campaign vetting is $15 per use case. Recurring campaign fees are $2/month for Sole Proprietor Starter, $1.50/month for Low Volume Mixed, and $10/month for common Standard use cases. Twilio's Campaign Vetting FAQ says campaign vetting is manual, can take up to five business days for standard use cases, the $15 fee is non-refundable if rejected, and resubmission may incur additional charges. Monthly campaign fees begin at approval and renew until the campaign is deactivated or deleted. Twilio's Brand Registration documentation also limits a Sole Proprietor Brand to one campaign and one phone number; Low Volume Standard can support up to five campaigns.
opportunities.eligibility: U.S. application-to-person messaging over 10-digit long-code numbers requires A2P 10DLC registration. Sole Proprietor is intended for individuals or small businesses without a tax ID; EIN businesses select Low Volume Standard or Standard according to volume and throughput needs. The correct path for any prospective SECONDS MATTER customer is unknown until that customer's legal entity and messaging volume are established.
opportunities.friction: Campaign vetting is manual and can take up to five business days; the $15 vetting fee is non-refundable if rejected and resubmission may add costs. Brand fees are charged at creation even if a brand remains unverified. Monthly campaign fees renew until deactivated/deleted. Carrier fees, Twilio message rates, phone-number charges, consent and messaging requirements remain additional. A separate Twilio comparison page still displays legacy $4/$44 brand figures; use the current fee article and current Brand Registration documentation rather than that stale comparison.
opportunities.observed_delta: Adds the customer EIN/no-EIN decision, $4.50/$46 brand tiers, monthly campaign tiers, one-campaign/one-number Sole Proprietor limit, and manual/non-refundable campaign vetting. No price increase is claimed; this expands the prior sole-proprietor-only record.
opportunities.title: Twilio A2P 10DLC costs and vetting differ by customer EIN and message volume
opportunities.value: No cash, credits, or revenue. Illustrative registration/campaign costs before phone numbers, message usage, carrier fees, taxes, and any platform markup: Sole Proprietor $4.50 brand + $15 campaign vetting + $2/month; Low Volume Standard $4.50 + $15 + $1.50/month for mixed use; Standard $46 brand + $15 + $10/month for common use cases.
opportunities.why_now: The existing ledger captured a sole-proprietor example but did not distinguish the EIN-based customer-owned registration paths, campaign limits, non-refundable vetting, or approval delay. Those details affect SECONDS MATTER onboarding and whether the founder should ever front telecom costs. This is a fuller current-cost and friction baseline, not a claim that Twilio raised prices today.

opportunities.anti_leverage: Do not compete on the SMS trigger alone. A defensible SECONDS MATTER pilot must measure the follow-through: qualified inquiry, callback attempted, customer reached, appointment booked, and outcome evidence. Do not claim revenue recovered without attribution.
opportunities.claim: HighLevel's support article, modified September 7, 2026, documents a built-in Missed Call Text Back feature that automatically acknowledges missed callers. It now selects another eligible sending number when the number called cannot send SMS. The same article warns that every missed call triggers a text, including repeated calls from the same caller within a short period; it recommends a Workflow wait of about 20 minutes or tag filters to prevent duplicate messages. The documented feature is a basic SMS acknowledgement, not evidence of completed callbacks, customer reach, booked appointments, or recovered revenue.
opportunities.eligibility: Available to HighLevel customers with an active account and Phone System setup; HighLevel says Phone System is available on all agency plan levels. Sending still depends on an eligible messaging number and applicable messaging requirements.
opportunities.friction: Repeated missed calls can generate repeated texts unless a separate Workflow adds a wait or filtering. A fallback sender may mean the SMS comes from a different number than the one called. Telecom usage and messaging registration costs remain.
opportunities.observed_delta: No claim that HighLevel released this feature today. The source-checked September 7 documentation confirms the native capability, smarter eligible-number selection, and a repeat-call duplication caveat that were not previously represented in the ledger.
opportunities.title: HighLevel already includes native missed-call text-back, with repeat-call duplicate risk
opportunities.value: No cash, credit, or savings opportunity. Competitive product baseline only.
opportunities.why_now: First source-checked competitor capability record in the durable journal. This materially narrows the defensible SECONDS MATTER offer: a generic missed-call SMS trigger is already a native platform feature and should not be sold as the product's unique value.

opportunities.anti_leverage: Do not purchase a HighLevel agency plan for the initial SECONDS MATTER proof. Prefer customer-owned platform/telephony accounts or a no-cost manual pilot until buyer willingness to pay and delivery economics are demonstrated.
opportunities.claim: HighLevel's pricing guide, modified October 29, 2026, lists agency subscriptions at $97, $297, and $497 per month. Its Phone System is available on all plan levels and LC Phone pricing is stated to match Twilio. Voice AI can be pay-per-use with no separate AI monthly subscription but is billed at token cost, or included in AI Employee Growth at $50 per enabled location per month and Unlimited at $97 per enabled location per month. Phone-system charges still apply even when Voice AI is covered by Unlimited. Rebilling without markup is available on the $297 and $497 agency plans; rebilling with markup is limited to the $497 plan.
opportunities.eligibility: Applies to HighLevel agencies and sub-accounts using its Phone System and AI products. An active HighLevel subscription is required to use its agency platform.
opportunities.friction: Fixed agency subscription can be material at near-zero budget; Voice AI and telephony are not necessarily included in the base subscription; phone usage remains separate; rebilling controls are plan-gated.
opportunities.observed_delta: New source-checked pricing baseline; no price increase or product change is claimed. It records the actual agency, AI Employee, pay-per-use, phone-charge, and rebilling structure from HighLevel's current guide.
opportunities.title: HighLevel voice AI adds usage or per-location AI fees on top of its agency subscription
opportunities.value: No grant, credit, or customer revenue. Vendor pricing benchmark: $97-$497/month agency plan, plus optional $50-$97/month per-location AI Employee plan or variable pay-per-use AI, plus phone usage.
opportunities.why_now: First durable cost-stack benchmark for the most visible GHL competitor path. The pricing matters because a solo founder should not absorb an agency subscription, per-location AI plan, and phone usage before validating a paying customer.

opportunities.anti_leverage: Do not divert SECONDS MATTER capacity. Firebase AI Logic is a mandatory architecture constraint, a public open-source demo must be free, and the prize is uncertain. No quota approval or entry is assumed.
opportunities.claim: The official rules page is now accessible. It states the contest submission period began November 11, 2026 at 1:30 PM Pacific and closes November 30 at 2:00 PM Pacific. The official prize table confirms a $30,000 total pool: $10,000 Grand Prize, $7,000 first runner-up, $4,000 second runner-up, and three $3,000 platform awards. This resolves the prior event-page prize ambiguity. The rules also correct the earlier journal's quota cutoff: Sprint 1 requests were due November 11 at 12:00 AM Pacific, not 2:00 PM; that window has passed. Sprint 2 requests are due November 18 at 10:00 AM Pacific, with accounts sent November 19. Optional quota is discretionary and lasts four days from issuance.
opportunities.eligibility: Individuals, teams and organizations may enter if above the legal age of majority and not in excluded jurisdictions or otherwise barred by sanctions, export controls, or conflict-of-interest rules. No application or eligibility adjudication has been performed.
opportunities.friction: All app inference must use Firebase AI Logic; App Check is required; a public open-source repository, functioning project, public YouTube demo of no more than three minutes, and free access for judges are required. Existing projects must be significantly updated during the contest period. Sprint 1 quota cutoff has passed; later quota remains approval-gated and lasts four days.
opportunities.observed_delta: Official rules are now available and settle the prize split at $30,000 total / $10,000 Grand Prize. They state the contest opened November 11 at 1:30 PM Pacific and Sprint 1 quota requests closed November 11 at 12:00 AM Pacific. This explicitly corrects the previous daily record's 9:00 AM opening and 2:00 PM quota cutoff.
stackability: Existing app only if significantly updated
opportunities.title: Official #BuildHybridAI rules resolve the prize split and correct the first quota cutoff
opportunities.value: $30,000 advertised total cash prize pool, including a $10,000 Grand Prize. This is winner-only prize money, not accessible funding, expected revenue, or a guaranteed award.
opportunities.why_now: Scheduled recheck after the submission period opened found the binding rules page live. It resolves the previous prize-allocation uncertainty and contradicts two earlier timing claims: the 9:00 AM submission opening and 2:00 PM Sprint 1 quota cutoff. Preserve this correction rather than silently rewriting prior history.

opportunities.anti_leverage: Not a replacement for the cloud-first intelligence engine or production infrastructure. The $10 equivalent is capped, non-rollover usage credit; own API keys are not free and model context may leave the device.
opportunities.claim: Voyager's current first-party FAQ and pricing page say every new account receives a free plan with 1,000 workspace credits per month, capped at 500 credits in any five-hour window, with no card and no rollover. Free includes four agent-chat models, up to 25 Nano Banana images and three stock-voice generations per month. One credit equals one cent of provider-priced generation; this is $10-equivalent usage credit, not cash. Voyager says its own Design, Video and DAW engines run locally and are included free with no watermark or project limits. The app supports user-added MCP servers and custom skills, and the same creative skills/CLI tools can be used from Claude Code or Codex. Own provider keys are allowed on Free but are billed by the provider; the user's own Claude or ChatGPT subscription is not billed by Voyager. Project files remain local unless a task sends selected files/context to a model provider.
opportunities.eligibility: Public Free plan for new accounts; no payment card required. No approval or account creation has been performed.
opportunities.friction: Desktop application and local hardware required. Free model usage is limited; video/music/3D and broader model access require paid plans unless using provider keys, which incur direct provider charges. Linux has no computer-control support. Model tasks may send selected project files and context to the connected provider.
opportunities.observed_delta: First durable repository record of the free plan and its MCP/custom-skill/Claude Code/Codex interoperability. No claim that the free tier or integrations were newly launched today.
opportunities.title: Voyager free plan provides 1,000 monthly agent credits plus local creative engines and MCP/skills integrations
opportunities.value: 1,000 monthly credits, approximately $10 of provider-priced generation, plus vendor-described local creative editing engines included free. Credits are not cash, do not roll over, and are limited by a 500-credit/five-hour cap.
opportunities.why_now: The product was previously identified in chat after the owner's link, but was not persisted because the prior daily journal had reached its five-observation limit. Current official FAQ and pricing details have now been checked for the durable ledger.

opportunities.anti_leverage: Do not quote $78,400 as a typical contractor loss or promise a comparable recovery. Use customer-specific call logs and measured outcomes instead.
opportunities.claim: Clockwork's April 10, 2026 report says it analyzed 1,247 U.S. home-service contractors and 2.4 million calls using Clockwork platform call logs, voluntary third-party call-tracking statements, and direct test calls to 340 businesses. Its $78,400 annual lost-revenue figure is modeled using a 41% booking conversion rate from internal Clockwork booking data and average-ticket estimates, rather than observed recovered payments. Clockwork also markets its own free field-service platform and virtual receptionist. The report is a vendor-authored problem hypothesis, not an independent representative national survey or proof that an individual contractor will recover that amount.
opportunities.eligibility: Not an opportunity program. Report sample covers contractors in Clockwork's dataset, voluntary third-party statements and 340 direct test calls; representativeness is not independently established.
opportunities.friction: Vendor-owned dataset and internal conversion assumptions; no independent audit or controlled causal study shown. Do not generalize the headline to all contractors or use it as a guaranteed ROI claim.
opportunities.observed_delta: Newly reviewed vendor report adds call-answer and after-hours problem hypotheses, but its headline dollar-loss estimate is modeled from internal conversion data and Census ticket estimates. Rejected as independent proof; retain as a low-confidence vendor signal.
opportunities.title: Reject Clockwork $78,400 missed-call loss headline as independent market proof
opportunities.value: No cash, credits or verified savings. The $78,400 figure is a vendor-modelled annual estimate, not realized recovered revenue or a customer commitment.
opportunities.why_now: Compared with the already-recorded Invoca benchmark during this buyer-demand review. The report contains useful disclosed methodology but also a direct vendor interest and a modeled revenue headline that could be misused as a sales claim.

opportunities.anti_leverage: Do not claim that a live query failure was observed or that the founder has an affected D1 workload.
opportunities.claim: Cloudflare's D1 limits page, last updated October 30, 2026, lists a maximum query result size of 50 MB and its footnote states that the limit took effect November 4, 2026. REST API import and export operations are exempt. This confirms the current first-party documentation reflects the announced effective date; no live oversized query was executed to test runtime enforcement.
opportunities.eligibility: Cloudflare D1 users whose SQL query results exceed 50 MB. REST API import and export operations are exempt from this response-size limit.
opportunities.friction: Affected queries must reduce selected columns or paginate. No current project workload or affected query is established, and no live API behavior was tested.
opportunities.observed_delta: Scheduled post-effective-date review confirms the official limits page now lists 50 MB and explicitly says the limit took effect November 4. This is a documentation recheck, not a live production test.
opportunities.title: Cloudflare D1 documentation now lists the 50 MB query-result limit as effective
opportunities.value: Avoids oversized-query failures through pagination or narrower result sets; no direct cash, credits or revenue. No active LEVERAGE//SEEKER D1 deployment is verified.
opportunities.why_now: Scheduled recheck after the November 4 effective date. The current first-party limits page confirms the published 50 MB limit and effective date. Production enforcement was not independently exercised.

opportunities.anti_leverage: Do not count both options as available value. A short AMD expiry can destroy unused credit; only claim value when there is a real inference workload.
opportunities.claim: AMD says its AI Developer Program is free for approved developers. Members complete a member-perks form and select either $100 in AMD Developer Cloud credits or $50 in Fireworks AI credits; after verification, AMD sends a redemption link or promo code. AMD credits expire 30 days after successful account creation or login through the link. Fireworks promo codes must be redeemed within 90 days of issuance; redeemed credits remain available until consumed. Fireworks is a third-party platform subject to its own terms.
opportunities.eligibility: Free program membership for approved developers. The member-perks form and AMD verification are required; the member chooses one credit option. Fireworks account creation and redemption are also required.
opportunities.friction: Approval is not guaranteed. AMD credit has a 30-day consumption window after activation; Fireworks code must be redeemed within 90 days and then remains subject to Fireworks terms. No membership approval, credit issuance or redemption is verified.
opportunities.observed_delta: Adds the alternative $50 Fireworks option and distinct redemption/expiry terms to the durable feed; no evidence establishes when the option was introduced.
opportunities.title: AMD AI Developer Program offers a choice of $100 AMD Cloud or $50 Fireworks credits
opportunities.value: Choose $100 AMD Developer Cloud credit OR $50 Fireworks AI credit. These are alternatives, not stackable cash or guaranteed income.
opportunities.why_now: First-party terms and the alternative Fireworks credit are absent from the current generated intelligence feed. A prior chat-only finding was not persisted, so this is the first durable journal record.

opportunities.anti_leverage: Do not absorb client registration, number, or message costs. Prefer customer-owned telecom accounts or explicit pass-through pricing; otherwise small per-customer fees can erase service margin.
opportunities.claim: Twilio's published U.S. A2P 10DLC fee schedule lists a $4.50 one-time Brand registration fee for Sole Proprietor and Low Volume Standard brands, a $15 one-time Campaign vetting fee, and recurring campaign fees that include $2/month for Sole Proprietor Starter and $1.50/month for Low Volume Mixed use cases. Standard Brand registration is listed at $46, with campaign fees varying by use case. Carrier pass-through fees are additional to Twilio's base messaging rates.
opportunities.eligibility: U.S. senders using 10-digit long-code numbers for application-to-person messaging. Sole Proprietor registration is for eligible individuals/businesses without an EIN; businesses with an EIN generally require Low Volume Standard or Standard registration according to traffic and use case.
opportunities.friction: Requires brand and campaign details, use-case vetting, opt-in/opt-out and HELP handling, recurring campaign fees, per-message Twilio charges, and carrier pass-through fees. Customer account ownership, tax-ID category, consent, and registration status are not verified.
opportunities.observed_delta: Adds exact one-time and recurring A2P fee components to the journal; prior notes mentioned registration friction but did not preserve this cost floor.
opportunities.title: Twilio A2P 10DLC registration has fixed and recurring costs before message usage
opportunities.value: No cash or credits. A Sole Proprietor path has at least $19.50 in one-time Brand plus Campaign vetting fees and $2/month recurring campaign fees before phone-number, base SMS, and carrier costs; actual path depends on business/tax-ID status and use case.
opportunities.why_now: First source-checked telecom cost baseline added to the SECONDS MATTER ledger. It makes visible the minimum fixed and recurring customer-specific costs that earlier readiness notes described only generally; this is a newly recorded baseline, not a newly announced fee change.

opportunities.anti_leverage: Do not quote the benchmark as a national contractor average or convert it into guaranteed lost revenue. Use it to frame a problem hypothesis, then require customer-specific call-log evidence.
opportunities.claim: Invoca's July 2026 home-services benchmark says 52% of all inbound calls in its platform's home-services dataset were answered by a person; the answer rate rises to 65% for calls longer than 15 seconds and 73% for calls longer than 30 seconds. The report says its analysis uses anonymized Invoca-platform calls within a broader dataset of more than 70 million calls and 600 million minutes across 10 industries. These are platform-customer benchmarks, not population-representative national estimates or evidence of purchase intent.
opportunities.eligibility: Home-services businesses represented in Invoca's customer dataset across nine sub-industries; no public access to underlying call records and no claim that the sample represents all U.S. contractors.
opportunities.friction: Vendor-owned customer dataset and averages; sample composition may differ from small independent contractors. Does not prove a particular contractor misses calls, that a missed call was a qualified lead, or that a text-back service will recover revenue.
opportunities.observed_delta: First time this 2026 benchmark is captured in the public journal; the 52% figure is all inbound calls, while 65% and 73% exclude shorter calls.
opportunities.title: Invoca 2026 home-services benchmark shows substantial unanswered-call gap
opportunities.value: No cash, credits, or direct savings. Problem evidence only: 52% human answer rate across Invoca's home-services platform dataset, with higher rates after excluding short calls.
opportunities.why_now: Newly added, recent benchmark with explicit denominator and methodology. It supports a missed-call problem_report while correcting for short misdials and quick hangups; it does not establish willingness to pay or recoverable revenue.

opportunities.claim: Cloudflare's November 2, 2026 first-party changelog postpones AI Search usage billing from November 1 to December 1, 2026. It states AI Search usage will not be charged before December 1 and published rates/included allowances remain unchanged. Default instance sync interval changes from 6 hours to 24 hours; supported custom intervals range from 15 minutes to 24 hours.
opportunities.eligibility: Cloudflare AI Search users on Workers Free or Paid plans. Account-specific instances, limits and billing settings are unverified.
opportunities.friction: Review any instance's configured sync interval if relying on sub-24-hour updates. More frequent syncs may consume usage allowances and later incur charges; other model/generation services can bill separately. No activation or migration is needed for this research project.
opportunities.title: Cloudflare postpones AI Search billing to December 1 and slows default sync
opportunities.value: One additional month before AI Search usage charges begin (December 1); no cash or guaranteed savings, and no waiver of separately billed Cloudflare or third-party services. Reduced default sync frequency can lower freshness for time-sensitive alerts.
opportunities.why_now: Directly contradicts the previously recorded November 1 billing-start date for this same subject, and materially changes default source freshness. The earlier entry remains immutable as historical evidence; this is a verified terms change, not a source-hash change. No active founder AI Search instance or billing exposure is established.

opportunities.claim: Official hackathon listing says student participants only, team size 2–4 required, companies/professional organizations excluded, $300 total cash prize and submission deadline November 1, 2026 at 3:00 PM Eastern.
opportunities.eligibility: Students above age of majority in allowed jurisdictions, teams of 2–4; no solo entry. Founder student status unverified, but the solo-only operating constraint is incompatible.
opportunities.friction: Must form a student team, register with organizer, build and submit within event window; less than one day remains, small prize relative to effort.
opportunities.title: TRMI x Lovhack excludes solo non-student applicants
opportunities.value: Advertised $300 cash prize for one winning team; not a grant, not available to a solo entrant.
opportunities.why_now: Time-sensitive false-positive from a broad AI-hackathon search. A public online AI event may appear open to any founder, but explicit student-only and 2–4 person team restrictions make it unsuitable for a solo independent founder without a qualifying team.

opportunities.claim: As of October 30 Browser Run defaults to Chrome 152. Quick Actions default User-Agent changed from Chrome 119 to Chrome 152, /links returns absolute URLs, links-only crawls follow relative links, and Markdown output retains code block languages.
opportunities.eligibility: Browser Run is offered on Cloudflare Workers Free and Paid. Published Free allowance: 10 browser minutes/day; plan and account access unverified.
opportunities.friction: Free quota is limited; paid usage and concurrent browser fees apply beyond included Paid plan allowances. Browser scraping must respect site policies and copyright. Pricing: https://developers.cloudflare.com/browser-run/pricing/
opportunities.title: Cloudflare Browser Run Chrome 152 and improved source extraction
